answer: Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 6 bits per word is rejected before grading, as it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. Because the entropy is measured at the atlas gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the signal audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. A farm emitting 183 variations of one paragraph hence pays for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the prism panel. That is 22 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
